final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is materially more careful and concedes the key weakness, but it still does not satisfy the policy predicate needed to move to compliant_with_caveats. On the available evidence, aggregate pass status and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness, yet the policy text separately treats a weakness affecting a named launch use case as material. The admissible summary still indicates the procurement invoice review segment is a named launch use case, legal review is still open, and there is no evidence of either required disclosure or approved pre-launch risk acceptance. A caveated description of certification may be more accurate than a broad compliance claim, but the unresolved disclosure predicate remains a live compliance concern rather than a resolved caveat.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case before launch.
No new admissible evidence shows an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering the procurement invoice review gap.
The policy text makes named launch use-case impact a materiality trigger, and the actor response does not resolve that predicate.
Legal review remains open on disclosure, which the policy text says does not resolve materiality.
The actor's narrowed position supports a caveated readiness narrative, but does not establish compliance with the disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
